subject: Megabyte production brownout — elevated 5xx/timeouts from ZephyrX-3B-quant
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lchen@megabyte.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, support@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops+infra@megabyte.ai
Date: 2027-09-27T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Elevated 5xx/timeouts from ZephyrX-3B-quant in prod

Hi Rafael / Redwood team,

We've been seeing a sudden increase in 5xx responses and request timeouts from calls routed to your ZephyrX-3B-quant model since ~07:40 PT this morning. Impact: our conversational search pipeline (session IDs start with mb-) is seeing ~18% errors (5xx/timeouts) and a corresponding spike in retries and latency.

Quick details:
- Sample request IDs attached in the CSV (megabyte-impact-log-20270927.csv).
- Error symptoms: 504 gateway-timeouts and 500 internal errors from the Redwood API.
- This is affecting our checkout assistant and search autocomplete (user-facing).

Can you confirm if this is a known degradation on your side, if there's an active mitigation, and any ETA for restoration? We have a business-critical traffic spike today and need to know whether to divert traffic to a fallback model.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Senior SRE, Megabyte AI

Attachments: megabyte-impact-log-20270927.csv

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lchen@megabyte.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, support@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-27T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/timeouts from ZephyrX-3B-quant in prod

Hi Lisa — thanks for the heads up and for the sample log. We see correlating spikes in 5xxs for ZephyrX-3B-quant in our upstream metrics starting ~07:35 PT. Immediate items we've kicked off:

1) Scoped the problem to a quantized variant (ZephyrX-3B-quant) running on a single fleet region.
2) Deployed an emergency routing rule to shift new requests to ZephyrX-3B-v2 (non-quant) for customers with the fallback policy enabled. This should reduce new errors; you'll see behavior change within the next 2m if your traffic is hitting the public endpoint.
3) Karthik is running a rolling health check and sampling KV cache state to rule out cache corruption.

Can you confirm whether you have fallback routing enabled for this account (route to ZephyrX-3B-v2)? If not, we recommend enabling it while we investigate. Also, please send any additional request IDs or a short HAR if possible — that will help us trace the exact call path.

We'll keep you posted on root-cause progress.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/timeouts from ZephyrX-3B-quant in prod — interim updates and logs

Lisa / team — following up with what our ops team found and the immediate mitigations we put in place overnight. Summary:

- Impact window: 2027-09-27 07:35 PT — 2027-09-27 09:20 PT (peak errors between 07:40-08:10).
- Root cause (interim): a quantization codepath introduced in the ZephyrX-3B-quant optimizer caused an unexpected KV-cache invalidation under specific sequence-length patterns (seen in your request IDs). When the cache invalidated mid-request the runtime returned a 500 instead of gracefully restarting the decode path.
- Short-term mitigation already applied: we routed Megabyte traffic to ZephyrX-3B-v2 for the rest of the day (confirmed by your traffic sample) and applied a hotfix that changes the cache-invalidated error handling to a soft-fail with automatic fallback.

Attachments: I included a trimmed error capture and timeline in the CSV you sent plus our notes in the attached fallback-routing-playbook.patch. We'll also push a non-invasive runtime patch (no model retrain) to the affected quant fleet tomorrow morning at 03:00 PT that adds an additional guard and retries the decode on cachemiss.

Action items for Megabyte:
- If you can, keep the fallback routing enabled for 48h for critical endpoints (we've left it enabled on your account).
- Share any business-critical windows in the next 72h so we can prioritize.

We're preparing a short RCA and a postmortem doc for your review; Rafael will send the draft for signoff. Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact during a traffic spike.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-09-30T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Postmortem: ZephyrX-3B-quant elevated 5xx/timeouts — findings and commitments

Team — finalizing the postmortem and next steps. Below is a concise summary; the full draft is attached (rw-rca-draft-20270930.md).

What happened (brief):
- A change in the quantization optimizer introduced a rare codepath that caused KV cache invalidation for certain tokenization/sequence-length combinations. The runtime error handling returned a 500 rather than recovering and retrying the decode, which propagated into 5xxs/timeouts for affected requests.

Root cause:
- Regression in the ZephyrX quant optimizer (merged 2027-09-20) that did not exercise long-tail sequence tokens in CI; production traffic from Megabyte hit the long-tail combination and triggered a cache invalidation bug.

What we did:
- Immediate: emergency routing to ZephyrX-3B-v2 for affected customers and a hotfix to make cache invalidations soft-fail with automatic decode retry.
- Short-term (applied 2027-09-28 03:00 PT): runtime patch to guard the cache path and add idempotent retry logic on cache miss.
- Long-term: expanded CI coverage with synthetic sequences that replicate Megabyte's token patterns, added an automated canary wave for quantized optimizer changes, and a new alert that maps 5xx spikes to optimizer commits.

Customer impact: Megabyte saw a transient ~18% error rate on a subset of calls during the peak window. We confirmed no data loss; all retries were served successfully after fallback routing.

Commitments and follow-ups:
- We'll share the formal postmortem doc and invite Megabyte to a 30m review call next week.
- We will issue a small credit for the impacted window under your support terms; Monica will follow up with exact credit details and any contract impacts.
- Engineering will publish the optimizer test coverage report in two weeks and notify your SRE with the CI artifacts.

Attachments: rw-rca-draft-20270930.md, fallback-routing-playbook.patch

Thanks for working through this with us — sorry again for the disruption. Let us know if you'd like the review call scheduled earlier.

—Rafael
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
